names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 7 Δεκεμβρίου, «Άγιοι Εξήκοντα Ιερείς», with the rank word left off.

names.form: Мученики 62 иерея и 300 мирян, в Африке от ариан пострадавшие
names.note: The heading of days.pravoslavie.ru’s name page and life page for 8 декабря ст. ст., kept whole because it is the whole company's name and this company has no personal one: the calendar counts the priests and the laymen and names nobody. «Мученики» is the rank and stays because without it the string is a bare pair of numbers. The form covers all three of the folders this line is read onto, which is why each of the three carries it.

death.note: **Two books, two rulers and two regnal brackets; the interval holds both, and it was 474–476 before this reading.** saint.gr: «μαρτύρησαν στην Καρχηδόνα στα χρόνια του βασιλιά Ζήνωνα (474 - 476 μ.Χ.)» — the years of the emperor Zeno, whose reign that page brackets 474 to 476. The Охридски пролог за 8. децембар ст. ст.: „Пострадали од јеретика аријеваца у време владе краља вандалскога Гунерика или Гензерика (477-484)“ — in the reign of the Vandal king Hunneric, or Genseric, bracketed 477 to 484. Neither bracket is a year either book gives for the martyrdom itself; both are reigns, and the bounds here are the union of the two. Nothing is chosen.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 8 декабря ст. ст. — «Мчч. 62-х иереев и 300 мирян, в Африке от ариан пострадавших (477).»

attestations.note: **ONE RUSSIAN LINE, THREE EXISTING FOLDERS, AND THE ARITHMETIC IS THE SOURCE'S OWN.** The line counts sixty-two priests and three hundred laymen; its life page then breaks the sixty-two down — «Из 62 иереев двух сожгли, остальным отрезали языки» — two of the sixty-two were burned and the rest had their tongues cut out. Two burned plus sixty with their tongues cut is the sixty-two, and those are precisely the two groups the Ohrid Prologue counts in its own body for this same menologion day, which is where `two-priests-of-carthage` and this folder come from: „Два свештеника сажежена, шездесеторици језици одрезани“. This folder is the sixty whose tongues were cut out, and the same row goes on `two-priests-of-carthage` and on `three-hundred-martyrs-of-africa`, each with its own share of the line named. `dates` UNTOUCHED: the line's «(477)» falls inside the 474–484 this folder already holds out of two regnal brackets, and a third book giving one year inside the interval is not a reason to narrow it.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (2 October 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 7ης Δεκεμβρίου — «Άγιοι Εξήκοντα Ιερείς»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 7 Δεκεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The company enumerates nobody — the sixty priests are counted and not named — so by the settled rule it is one folder. The page names no magistrate here, only Zeno's reign, where the neighbouring entry for the two priests adds Honorichos the Arian. No hymn is printed. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 21.12.2025 (8. децембар ст. ст.) — „Свети мученици у Африци.“

attestations.note: The second of the three groups the day’s third entry counts: «шездесеторици језици одрезани», sixty had their tongues cut out, which is this folder — sixty, counted and unnamed, with their tongues cut out, exactly as saint.gr keeps them on its 7 Δεκεμβρίου. The company heading „Свети мученици у Африци.“ is quoted whole on each of the three folders and is a true description of each. THE ONE THING THIS BOOK DOES NOT SAY IS THAT THEY WERE PRIESTS: it says «шездесеторици», sixty of them, where saint.gr heads them «Άγιοι Εξήκοντα Ιερείς», sixty priests, and the display name and the `presbyter` type on this folder are that page’s and are left exactly as they were. NO `sr` NAME FORM, the heading holding no personal name and its one company designation belonging to all three groups at once. `types` UNTOUCHED. `dates` WIDENED from 474–476 to 474–484 on the same two regnal brackets as the two priests — Zeno’s «(474 - 476 μ.Χ.)» against the Vandal king’s «(477-484)» — with nothing chosen. NO `locations`: Africa in this book, Carthage in that one. NO `related` row: neither book names one of them. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.
